aix432.notes: Framebuffer console only: AIX's LFT draws through the emulated Matrox GXT130P. The pointer is PS/2 relative on the wire (no tablet on a 40p) but ABSOLUTE to the daemon: AIX drives the Matrox HARDWARE cursor, so QEMU reads the guest's own pointer position back out of the DAC CURPOSX/Y registers and a closed loop inside hw/display/mga.c converges on the commanded pixel -- labctl 'abs x y' lands 1:1 and nothing dead-reckons. Keys still ride the QEMU/dbus path. Exec is telnet_unix_e: AIX's own telnetd on the retronet tap at 10.99.0.28:23, dialled from labhost only -- the AIXRN-IN containment chain still blocks every guest-originated packet, so the guest gained no reach. Reset restores the in-qcow2 'golden' snapshot, which skips the genuine IBM firmware's POST entirely -- a cold boot walks that POST and takes 15-25 minutes.

amix.notes: HOST-NATIVE: FS-UAE 3.2.35 (its OWN copy at assets/amix/fsuae-native, built from the merged source with fsuae-slirp-hostfwd.patch, FSUAE_STATION=amix) runs an Amiga 3000 (68030+MMU, Kickstart 2.04 r37.175) with an A2410 TIGA board on the host inside a pinned 1024x768 Xvfb; the guest's X -tiga server drives the board (OPEN LOOK, 256 colours) and the daemon captures the X root (SH_CAPTURE=x11). No QEMU/QMP, no exec channel (in.telnetd does listen on 23 inside the guest -- a cheap follow-up). POINTER: ABSOLUTE via the GUEST's X server (SH_INPUT_BACKEND=x11test + SH_X11TEST_MOTION=warp + SH_X11WARP_DISPLAY=127.0.0.1:72). The UAE mousehack is an AmigaOS trap AMIX never registers, so any XTEST motion is relative+accelerated there; instead the A2065 runs on slirp and the launcher adds a LOOPBACK-ONLY redirect 127.0.0.1:6072 -> 10.0.2.15:6000 (the board's X server listens on the same :0); the daemon warps (XWarpPointer) and reads back (XQueryPointer); buttons/keys ride XTEST into the Xvfb with each button edge held until the warp is confirmed. Single injector: never push motion at this guest by another path (no xdotool mousemove on the live Xvfb). The pointer is dead while the guest X server is (boot ~90 s; x11warp-check.log says ok / STALE GOLDEN / TIMED OUT). In RTG mode the capture is identity-mapped (no stretch, zoom only affects the boot console). Golden (unified 2026-09-01) carries the colour session, /etc/inet/hosts amix=10.0.2.15 + slirphost=10.0.2.2 (rc.inet brings aen0 up; NO default route), and xhost +slirphost in both /etc/kh-xsession and /etc/kh-xsession.mono. Reset=relaunch: cold boot of a fresh work HDF copied from disk/amix-system.hdf.golden; no statefile. Framebuffer-proven 2026-09-01 on the shipping binary at 1024x768: readback exact and sprite on target at 16 points incl. all four corners, residual 0 px; click and keys proven by guest response (docs/guests/amix.md). Launcher stations/amix/x11-runtime.sh.

hpuxvue.notes: exec = serial_shell: the golden bakes a LIVE root session on the guest's serial line (-sh on tty1p0, PS1 KHPROMPT>, reached on serial.sock in the station dir) -- there is NO getty to log in to, and Mosaic (a window of the exhibit scene) is a CHILD of that shell, so the client must never end the session. Client scripts/labctl.d/hpuxvueexec.py, no port, no password. MEASURED LIMIT: shell builtins are reliable (120/120 echo, 20/20 append+readback, 10/10 forking subshells) but running an EXTERNAL binary wedges the session about half the time, permanently -- the tty still echoes, nothing executes, and no getty respawns because init's respawn slot is held by the shell that is still there. exec reports a wedge as exit 125; the heal is `labctl reset hpuxvue` (loadvm golden), which also resets the visitor's scene, so it is the operator's call. A wedge does NOT stall the guest: the closed-loop pointer still converges exactly. See docs/guests/hpuxvue.md. POINTER ACCURACY: WITHIN 1 px, NOT EXACT. The Artist engine is a closed loop with ptr-deadband=1 and converges on abs(err) <= deadband on BOTH axes, so it is SPECIFIED to stop within one pixel -- `labctl abs x y` lands at x+/-1, y+/-1, converged and held. This is weaker than rhapsody's and macos753's exact landing: those use kh-ramabs, which has no deadband at all and tests literal equality, so 0 px is the correct strictness there and 1 px would hide a missed publish. Do not carry this tolerance to a ramabs station, and do not set ptr-deadband=0 to make a test pass -- the deadband is what stops the hunting that leaves window-border hotspots unmeasurable.
